COURSES.name: Spine & Spinal Lesions
COURSES.blurb: Spine MRI from the ground up: degenerative disease, the three compartments of spinal lesions, and the carotid space.

COURSES.name: Emergency & Brain Neuroimaging
COURSES.blurb: Emergency presentations of the head, neck, spine and brain, demyelinating disease, nerve entrapment, brain tumors and brain anatomy.

COURSES.name: Neurovascular & Musculoskeletal
COURSES.blurb: Neurovascular imaging, then the hip, shoulder and knee, closing with the pediatric musculoskeletal patient.

MODULES.d: 27 rare and challenging spine MRI cases, each reviewed with neurosurgeon-turned-neuroradiologist Malcolm Shupeck, MD.

MODULES.t: MRI Mastery Series: Degenerative Joint Disease (DJD)
MODULES.d: Current disc nomenclature, common herniation locations, surgical implications of disc injury, and more than a dozen DJD case reviews.

MODULES.t: MRI Mastery Series: Intradural Intramedullary Spinal Lesions
MODULES.d: Part one of the spinal lesions trilogy.

MODULES.t: MRI Mastery Series: Intradural Extramedullary Lesions (IDEM)
MODULES.d: Part two of the spinal lesions trilogy, focused largely on benign entities.
Part three: extradural etiologies that compress the dura and mimic intradural lesions.

MODULES.t: Imaging Mastery Series: The Carotid Space
MODULES.d: Carotid space disease and displacement patterns, head and neck anatomy, key differentials and clinical pearls.
The most common emergency department presentations, with 45 DICOM cases and pre- and post-tests.
Anatomy and imaging technique for demyelinating disorders, followed by review of nearly 30 cases.
Emergency brain presentations with 38 DICOM cases and pre- and post-tests.

MODULES.t: MRI Mastery Series: Nerve Imaging — Entrapment Neuropathy & Tumors
MODULES.d: Upper-extremity nerve MRI: protocol, phases and patterns of denervation, nerve pathway anatomy, and impingement, trauma, inflammatory and tumor cases.
Meningiomas and non-glial tumors: protocols, anatomic correlation and case review with neuroradiologist Benjamin LeSar, MD.
Surface anatomy, sulci and gyri, then each of the twelve cranial nerves.
Time-sensitive neurovascular cases, from critical to benign, with management insight from Malcolm Shupeck, MD.
SLAP lesions types I–X defined through diagrams, surgical video and MRI case review.
Pediatric imaging is not adult imaging in miniature: growth plates, ossification centers, and cartilage injury in children.

ROTATIONS.title: Interventional Pain Management
ROTATIONS.desc: Observe spinal procedures and learn the decision pathways behind them: when a patient is referred for intervention, and how conservative care fits before and after.

ROTATIONS.title: MRI Physics & Neuroradiology
ROTATIONS.desc: How the images are made and read: scan acquisition, slice thickness and diagnostic logic, applied through the program's ABCDE imaging interpretation method.

ROTATIONS.title: Orthopedic Extremity & Spine Surgery
ROTATIONS.desc: Separate hip from lumbar pathology and follow the surgeon's reasoning through the operative decision frameworks used in orthopedic spine and extremity care.

ROTATIONS.title: Neurosurgery & Emergency Medicine
ROTATIONS.desc: Real-world triage and patient flow, and the neurosurgical view of how urgent a spine case is and when it crosses a referral threshold.

ROTATIONS.title: Family & Internal Medicine
ROTATIONS.desc: Where spine complaints first show up: in primary care visits and within chronic disease management, and what that means for co-management.

ROTATIONS.title: Spine-Care Team Integration
ROTATIONS.desc: The capstone. Fellows work as the spine-care navigator on the interdisciplinary team, bridging conservative, interventional and surgical services.
